title: "Transforming a response"

The Provo regression response is a mean of log first-fixation durations. A **response transformation** changes the scale on which the model treats effects as additive. For a positive duration $T$, the course transformation is stated below.

We first identify the estimand created by logging before aggregation, then fit on that scale and translate predictions back to geometric-mean milliseconds.

$$
Y=\log T
$$

turns a multiplicative change in milliseconds into an additive change on the log scale.

## What the prepared response means

For position $i$, the course table stores a reader-aggregated mean log duration, $\overline{\log T}_i$. Exponentiating it gives

$$
G_i
=
\exp\!\left(\overline{\log T}_i\right),
$$

the geometric mean duration among the retained reader measurements for that position. It does not give the arithmetic mean duration.

For two positive reader durations $t_1$ and $t_2$, the arithmetic mean is $(t_1+t_2)/2$, while exponentiating the mean log duration gives

$$
\exp\left\{\frac{\log t_1+\log t_2}{2}\right\}
=\sqrt{t_1t_2}.
$$

These summaries are equal only when $t_1=t_2$. The order of operations thus matters: taking logs before averaging targets the geometric mean after exponentiation, whereas averaging raw milliseconds and then logging targets a different summary.

```{r}
#| label: transform-provo-response
library(ggplot2)

provo <- read.csv(
  "data/provo/content-word-positions.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
provo$cloze_surprisal_bits <- -log2(provo$OrthoMatchModel)
provo$cloze_surprisal_c <-
  provo$cloze_surprisal_bits - mean(provo$cloze_surprisal_bits)
provo$ffd_geometric_mean_ms <- exp(provo$mean_log_ffd)

fit <- lm(mean_log_ffd ~ cloze_surprisal_c, data = provo)
residual_sd <- summary(fit)$sigma

stopifnot(
  max(abs(
    log(provo$ffd_geometric_mean_ms) - provo$mean_log_ffd
  )) < 1e-12,
  all(provo$ffd_geometric_mean_ms > 0)
)

summary(provo$ffd_geometric_mean_ms)
```

Under the working model for the stored position summaries

$$
Y_i\mid x_i\sim\mathcal N(\mu_i,\sigma^2),
$$

two summaries of the back-transformed position response differ:

$$
\operatorname{Median}(T_i\mid x_i)=\exp(\mu_i)
$$

but

$$
\mathbb{E}[T_i\mid x_i]=\exp(\mu_i+\sigma^2/2).
$$

The second identity follows from the lognormal moment-generating calculation. Back-transforming a fitted log mean without the variance term thus targets a conditional median, or equivalently a geometric mean of the stored position response under this model, rather than its arithmetic mean.

From [expectations of functions](../random-variables-and-distributions/expectation-of-functions.qmd), if $Y\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, then its moment-generating function is $M_Y(t)=\exp(\mu t+\sigma^2t^2/2)$. Setting $t=1$ gives

$$
\mathbb{E}[e^Y]=M_Y(1)=\exp(\mu+\sigma^2/2).
$$

The identity thus depends on the normal working model for log responses; exponentiation alone does not supply the correction.

```{r}
#| label: plot-provo-response-transform
#| fig-cap: "Observed position-level geometric mean durations and two back-transformed summaries from the fitted log-scale model."
grid <- data.frame(
  cloze_surprisal_bits = seq(
    min(provo$cloze_surprisal_bits),
    max(provo$cloze_surprisal_bits),
    length.out = 160L
  )
)
grid$cloze_surprisal_c <-
  grid$cloze_surprisal_bits - mean(provo$cloze_surprisal_bits)
grid$mu <- predict(fit, newdata = grid)
grid$conditional_geometric_mean <- exp(grid$mu)
grid$working_lognormal_mean <- exp(grid$mu + residual_sd^2 / 2)

point_opacity <- 0.2
ggplot(provo, aes(cloze_surprisal_bits, ffd_geometric_mean_ms)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey65", alpha = point_opacity, size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(cloze_surprisal_bits, conditional_geometric_mean),
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = grid,
    aes(cloze_surprisal_bits, working_lognormal_mean),
    color = "black",
    linetype = 2,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Modeled cloze surprisal (bits)",
    y = "Position geometric mean FFD (ms)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

At the observed predictor center, the fitted geometric mean is `r sprintf("%.1f", exp(coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]]))` ms, while the working lognormal arithmetic mean of position-level geometric means is `r sprintf("%.1f", exp(coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]] + residual_sd^2 / 2))` ms. The small difference is computed from the actual Provo regression residual scale.

A potential worry is that this page diagnoses raw reader-time skew. It cannot. The prepared response has already averaged log duration by position, so the page demonstrates transformation and back-transformation of the stored summaries only.

## Recap and check your understanding

1. Why is `exp(mean_log_ffd)` a geometric mean?
2. Which raw-scale summary includes the $\sigma^2/2$ term?
3. Does a linear effect on log duration imply a constant millisecond difference?
4. Why can this table not reveal the raw reader-level distribution?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. `exp(mean_log_ffd)` equals $\exp(\overline{\log T})$, the geometric mean of the retained positive durations. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The conditional arithmetic mean under the lognormal working model is $\mathbb{E}[T\mid x]=\exp(\mu+\sigma^2/2)$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. No. A constant additive change on the log scale is a constant multiplicative ratio on the millisecond scale, so the millisecond difference depends on the baseline. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. The stored response already averages log durations over readers, so individual trial values and their distribution are unavailable. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
